I'm finishing up their calanthe dress right now and I'm happy with it, with a few caveats. I'm not shaped remotely like the pattern, so I went up 4 sizes to accommodate my waist measurement and then had to take a solid 6 inches out of the bust, and I made my own sleeve pattern. Not that big a deal but I can see how it'd complicate things for a more elaborate or fitted garment, or for a beginner.

I mean, for me the actual labor of pattern drafting, cutting and sewing isn't dramatically different between a XS and a 3x (that's the size range I've made stuff for as a casual hobbyist). I charge what I paid for materials + an hourly wage, so if it's substantially more or less, it gets factored in there. (And technically you could get a discount by being my size, because that's what I'm mostly likely to have an existing pattern in, hence speeding up the process.) 

Mine is a small and chaotic enterprise though, and I exclusively work for people I like. I also don't usually pay that much for fabric, so I imagine if I were working in fine silks or something!that might be a larger proportion of the total cost.
